summary: Break with the one you served: {former principal}, whom you served or backed for years, does something you will not defend, and the cameras wait for you.
realLife: One life: After January 6, 2021, he broke with the president he had served, ran against him in 2024, and declined to endorse him. Another: He helped Trump prepare for a 2020 debate, then broke with him over the 2020 result and ran against him in 2023. Another: She voted with Trump about 93 percent of the time, then broke with him after the Capitol attack.
gates: You served under or backed {former principal} on record.
{former principal} did something on record you oppose.
weights: How popular they are with your party.

branches.then: You are the first deputy in generations to run against the one you served, and you raise little.

branches.when: you helped them prepare, then broke
branches.then: They say your old scandal should be looked at again.

branches.when: you voted with them nearly every time
branches.then: After the break, your party treats those years of votes as nothing (C15).
